newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: US general in S.Korea says woman's murder "tragic".
newsitem.headline: US general in S.Korea says woman's murder "tragic".

text.p: The commander of U.S. military forces in South Korea on Saturday described as tragic the murder of a local woman for which an American serviceman is to be charged.
General John Tillely, who is also the commander of the Korea-U.S. Combined Forces, told reporters the killing of Lee Ki-sun, who was stabbed to death a week ago, was "tragic and nonsensical".
He said he believed the Korean police and U.S. military investigators would thoroughly probe the incident.

The U.S. military has said that Eric Munnich, from Chicago, is to be charged with the murder. It said in a statement that Munnich had confessed to the killing during questioning by South Korean police and U.S. military investigators.
The body of Lee, 44, was found on September 7 in a boarding house near a U.S. military base where Munnich is stationed.
Munnich is now detained at a U.S. military installation but will be imprisoned at a Korean jail if he is prosecuted and found guilty by Korean legal authorities, he added.
The United States maintains 37,000 troops in South Korea.
